svg.title: Reading order when an Ontario landlord objects to a pet
svg.desc: Flow chart. Start when a landlord objects. If the only objection is a no-pet clause in the tenancy agreement, Residential Tenancies Act section 14 makes that clause void, where the Act applies. A condo declaration, by-law, or rule is a separate document and can restrict pets. An application grounded on the animal under section 76 uses a notice under section 64, 65, or 66, and the Board must be satisfied. Damage notices are sections 62 and 63. The Landlord and Tenant Board decides. This chart is not a ruling.
svg.text: If a landlord objects, read in this order
Ontario only. Not a Board order. Checked 26 Sep 2026.
Lease clause only? RTA s.14: that no-pet provision is void
Only if the Act applies. Shared kitchen or bathroom with the owner can be s.5.
Condo declaration, by-law, or rule? Read it. s.14 does not erase it.
CAO guide: those documents may limit pets. The tribunal is a separate filing.
Notice under s.64, s.65, or s.66, grounded on the animal?
s.76: the Board must be satisfied. Damage notices are s.62 and s.63.
The Landlord and Tenant Board decides
A yes in one box does not answer the next box. A pet deposit is not on this chart. It is s.105 and s.106, not a second deposit.
Saving Optimizer. Education only. Confirm with the statute and the Board.
